Thanks for the forward, Ben. I took a quick pass on the prompt CSV and here are the recommended next steps and initial model suggestions: 

Initial recommendations (we'll produce a short eval report before Friday):
- Quality-first: redwood-13b-rlhf (quantized fp16) — expected best overall summaries on support transcripts.
- Latency/cost-first: redwood-7b-quant (8-bit) — lower cost with modest drop on subtle summarization quality.

What we'll run: 
- End-to-end eval on the attached prompt set (we'll simulate your 95th percentile dialog lengths using the length distribution column you provided).
- Metrics: ROUGE-L, semantic-similarity (embedding-based), hallucination rate (manual spot-check), and latency distribution across tokens.

Redaction guidance: 
- For Acme's retention rules, recommend client-side redaction on ingest for PII (emails, SSNs, account IDs) + token-level masking in our eval so that evaluation reflects production behavior. We can provide a redaction script and pattern list for your security team to review.

Deliverables and timeline: 
- By Thu EOD we’ll have a preliminary model-fit summary (high-level recommendations).
- By Fri 9am PT a short report with benchmark links and suggested config (batching, KV cache, quant profile).

Logan — can you confirm whether any of the edge-case examples will require special tokenization or prompt-engineering (e.g., multi-message context windows)?
